title: Rapiscan and Taronga/Macquarie CT algorithms detect shark fins, seahorses, and sea cucumbers at 86–96% in laboratory testing
summary: A vendor-affiliated CT study reported 86–96% detection of three marine-wildlife classes and 13% overall false alarms; testing used original scans and synthetic composites, with no customs outcome.
account: Pirotta and colleagues tested AI detection of marine wildlife in three-dimensional X-ray scans. Their June 8, 2026 paper reports 298 scans from 68 specimens, including preserved specimens and fresh shark material. The researchers expanded the scans by inserting specimen images into baggage images. A 512-bag test set contained both original scans and these synthetic composites, drawn from the same specimen population. Table 3 reports detection rates of 95% for shark fins, 96% for seahorses, and 86% for sea cucumbers. The overall false-alarm rate was 13%; the class-specific rates were 2%, 9%, and 1%. Rapiscan supplied equipment and funded staff participation in analysis and writing. The paper demonstrates laboratory detection, with no reported operational seizure or customs evaluation.
purpose: Automated detection of marine wildlife in CT scans of mail and luggage to support customs inspection; no operational evaluation is reported.
system: Rapiscan 3D X-ray CT marine-wildlife detection algorithms (3D convolutional neural networks with 3D Threat Image Projection)
model_version: Experimental 3D convolutional neural networks trained on CT scans and synthetic Threat Image Projection composites; no released model version reported
developer: Rapiscan Systems Ltd with Taronga Conservation Society Australia and Macquarie University
deployer: None; proof of concept with no customs authority deployment
location: Sydney, New South Wales, Australia (research setting)
segment: Security-screening vendor and conservation research partnership
taxonomy_note: Lab detection rates for trafficked wildlife are read as task performance; no seizure is documented.

ratings.reason: The paper reports no operational customs evaluation or documented seizure using these algorithms.
